stories.title: E-Trading Firm Octaura Signs on for Full Floor at 111 W. 33rd Street
stories.excerpt: Empire State Realty Trust, Inc. (ESRT) has signed Octaura Holdings LLC, an electronic trading, data & analytics provider, to a 28,914-square-foot office space on the entire 17th floor at 111 W. 33rd St. Lease terms were not disclosed. “111 W. 33rd St. offers a workplace that supports companies with employee recruitment, retention and productivity,” said Ryan Kass, EVP, co-head of real estate and chief revenue officer at ESRT. “Octaura’s new lease reflects the demand for modern office space with exceptional transit access and amenities, and we are pleased to welcome them to our portfolio.” Neil Goldmacher and Cooper Weisman of Newmark represented Octaura in leasing negotiations. Shanae Ursini and Kerry Lavelle of ESRT and Scott Klau, Erik Harris and Neil Rubin of Newmark represented the property owner. In its third-quarter earnings report, released this week, ESRT said it posted funds from operations of 20 cents per share. The post E-Trading Firm Octaura Signs on for Full Floor at 111 W. 33rd Street appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Octaura Holdings leases 28,914 SF full floor at 111 W. 33rd St., Manhattan.
Fintech/trading firm signals confidence in Midtown South office market and transit access.
ESRT achieves 91.9% occupancy in Q3 2026, up 280 bps QoQ.
stories.summary: Octaura Holdings, an electronic trading and data analytics firm, signed a 10-year lease for the entire 17th floor (28,914 SF) at Empire State Realty Trust's 111 W. 33rd Street in Midtown South at $81/SF asking rent. The deal reflects tenant appetite for modern office space with superior transit connectivity and amenities. ESRT's office portfolio reached 91.9% occupancy in Q3 2026, up from 89.1% in Q2.
stories.impact: Tech and fintech tenant demand for Midtown South office signals ongoing flight from outer boroughs and secondary markets; 111 W. 33rd's transit hub status (near Penn Station/Herald Square) is a competitive moat. For multifamily developers, this underscores continued job concentration in Manhattan core, supporting rent resilience in proximate residential corridors (Chelsea, Midtown West, Hell's Kitchen). However, office-to-residential conversion risk remains material in Midtown if office demand softens.

stories.title: Architecture Firm Corgan Expands to 41K SF at Empire State Building
stories.excerpt: Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) signed more than 28,600 square feet of leases at the Empire State Building in the third quarter of this year. In the largest deal, architecture firm Corgan signed a 12.4-year, 15,157-square-foot lease in the building in an expansion from its current 26,035 square feet, giving it a total footprint of 41,192 square feet at the landmarked office building, according to ESRT’s third-quarter earnings report. Meanwhile, supply chain finance firm Zenyth Advisors agreed to a new 11-year, 13,459-square-foot lease, according to the landlord. ESRT did not immediately disclose the updated asking rents at the building, but asking rents were $96 per square foot as recently as July. Corgan’s expansion follows a series of renovations to its space on the 54th floor, which has helped the firm consolidate teams from other offices, Commercial Observer reported at the time. ESRT did not respond to a request for comment and it’s unclear who brokered the two deals. Other recent arrivals to the Empire State Building include Los Angeles-based United Talent Agency, which leased 100,948 square feet in July, as well as law firm Elsberg Baker & Maruri, which signed a 39,237-square-foot lease in July 2025. The real estate investment trust announced the deals Tuesday during its third-quarter earnings call with investors, in which it reported strong office sales and leasing. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Corgan architecture firm expands 58% to 41,192 SF at Empire State Building.
Firm consolidates teams post-renovation on 54th floor; 12.4-year lease signals long-term occupancy.
Zenyth Advisors leases 13,459 SF; total Q3 leasing 28,600+ SF at landmark.
stories.summary: Architecture firm Corgan expanded its footprint at the Empire State Building from 26,035 SF to 41,192 SF on a 12.4-year lease, following renovations to its 54th-floor space that enabled team consolidation. Supply chain finance firm Zenyth Advisors separately leased 13,459 SF on an 11-year term. ESRT did not disclose updated asking rents, though July rates were $96/SF.
stories.impact: Creative services and fintech tenant clustering in landmark NYC office buildings indicates sustained demand for prestigious addresses despite remote-work trends. For multifamily developers, this reinforces that high-wage professional services and tech workers remain concentrated in Manhattan's iconic submarkets, supporting rental demand and pricing power in adjacent residential neighborhoods (Flatiron, Kips Bay, Stuyvesant Town area).

stories.title: Faris Lee Continues Breakup Strategy at Lakewood Center with $37M Sale
stories.excerpt: Continuing the execution of a breakup strategy at Lakewood Center in Lakewood, Faris Lee Investments has closed a $37.3- million sale consisting of 97,319 square feet of retail, featuring Burlington, 24 HR Fitness and Bank of America. This is the second large portion of Lakewood Center that Faris Lee has sold this year- culminating in a total of $76 Million. Faris Lee Investments represented the seller, a consortium of multiple owners. The transaction was led by managing principals Don MacLellan and Jeff Conover, senior managing director Scott DeYoung, and director Greg Lukosky Prior to close of escrow, the ownership negotiated lease extensions on the major anchors, a further testament to the quality of the real estate. “Transactions of this caliber require a deep understanding of both the real estate and the investment objectives of the buyer,” said MacLellan. “Lakewood Center is an exceptional retail destination, and the opportunity to acquire three strong national tenants in such a supply-constrained Southern California location is extremely compelling.” The post Faris Lee Continues Breakup Strategy at Lakewood Center with $37M Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Faris Lee closes $37.3M sale of Lakewood Center retail portfolio in Los Angeles.
Sale includes Burlington, 24 HR Fitness, Bank of America anchors; second major exit this year.
Ownership negotiated lease extensions with major tenants prior to close of escrow.
stories.summary: Faris Lee Investments closed a $37.3 million sale of 97,319 SF of retail space at Lakewood Center in Lakewood, California, anchored by Burlington, 24 HR Fitness, and Bank of America. This is the second large parcel Faris Lee has divested this year, totaling $76 million in sales. The ownership secured lease extensions with major anchors before closing.
stories.impact: Breakup and sale of class-B suburban retail centers reflects asset recycling in low-growth physical retail; supply-constrained Southern California retail fundamentals are supporting buyer demand. For multifamily developers in LA metro, this signals continued retail underperformance and mixed-use risk—favor density, density, and strong anchor tenants (not fashion/discretionary retail). The Lakewood submarket's stability attracted institutional buyers, but retail dependence constrains multifamily yields in strip centers.

stories.title: Wells Fargo Supplies $133M Refi for Miami-Dade Industrial Campus
stories.excerpt: LBA Realty has secured refinancing for an industrial campus near the edge of Miami-Dade County, property records show. Wells Fargo provided the $133 million financing backing the 37-acre Dolphin Commerce Center. The bank increased by $83 million a 2022 loan with $50 million of outstanding debt, according to mortgage documents. The 709,480-square-foot property features five warehouses between 11200 and 11698 Northwest 25th Street in Sweetwater, about a mile north of the Dolphin Mall, east of the Florida Turnpike, near the border with the Everglades National Park. Constructed in the late 1990s, the property features clear heights ranging between 24 and 28 feet. About 36,000 square feet of warehouse space remains available, according to a listing on LBA Realty’s website. In 2022, the Irvine, Calif.-based owner bought the campus for $198 million. The firm owns one other industrial property in South Florida, a 37,909-square-foot warehouse in Weston, which it purchased for $9 million in 2020. A representative for LBA Realty did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Wells Fargo provides $133M refi for 709,480 SF Dolphin Commerce Center in Miami-Dade.
LBA Realty increased 2022 loan by $83M; property carries 36,000 SF available vacancy.
Sweetwater industrial campus near Everglades border; clear heights 24–28 feet; late 1990s vintage.
stories.summary: Wells Fargo secured $133 million in refinancing for Dolphin Commerce Center, a 37-acre, 709,480 SF industrial campus in Sweetwater near the Miami-Dade/Everglades border. The lender increased the outstanding 2022 debt by $83 million. The five-warehouse property features clear heights of 24–28 feet and approximately 36,000 SF of available space.
stories.impact: Refinance uptick at Miami-Dade industrial assets signals lender confidence in logistics corridor fundamentals despite macro uncertainty. For multifamily developers, industrial-led logistics growth (e.g., distribution centers, 3PL) in Miami-Dade periphery (Sweetwater, Doral) correlates with population and job growth that supports residential demand; however, Dolphin Commerce Center's partial vacancy (5%) and distance from job centers (west of turnpike, near Everglades) offer limited direct labor-shed benefit. Monitor conversion of peripheral industrial submarkets to mixed-use residential as Miami urban core densifies.

stories.title: Apparel Brand American Giant Leases Brooklyn Store at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue
stories.excerpt: San Francisco-based apparel brand American Giant has arrived in Brooklyn. The manufacturer of sportswear and casual clothing made exclusively in the United States has signed a lease for 3,400 square feet at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue in North Williamsburg, where it will open its first Brooklyn store, according to a source familiar with the deal. The location between Kent and Wythe avenues secures American Giant a spot along Williamsburg’s increasingly popular waterfront corridor near Domino Park, as well as proximity to nearby North Sixth Street, where high-end brands like Rolex and Hermes host their borough flagships. Cornelia Street Partners’ Lenny Kohlmayer and Evan Kleinberg negotiated the lease on behalf of American Giant, while Flatiron Real Estate Advisors’ Steven Ancona represented the landlord entity, China Building. American Giant’s upcoming retail location will occupy 1,700 square feet of the space, according to a spokesperson for Cornelia Street Partners. American Giant has not disclosed plans for the remaining 1,700 square feet of its lease. The deal carries a 10-year term, and its asking rent was not disclosed. A recent deal inked by fashion retailer Zara at nearby 184-192 Bedford Avenue notched $450 per square foot for the ground floor, according to The Real Deal. Founded in 2011, American Giant currently operates a store in San Francisco and an outlet location in Smithfield, N.C., according to its website. A showroom in San Francisco is listed as temporarily closed, and the brand’s SoHo store, which opened at 339 West Broadway in 2024, has since ceased operations. American Giant and Ancona did not respond to requests for comment, and representatives for China Building could not be reached by press time. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: American Giant, San Francisco apparel brand, opens first Brooklyn store at 83-85 Metropolitan Ave.
3,400 SF lease (1,700 SF retail) in North Williamsburg waterfront corridor near Domino Park.
Location anchors Williamsburg retail strip alongside Rolex, Hermes; between Kent and Wythe avenues.
stories.summary: American Giant, a US-made apparel manufacturer based in San Francisco, signed a 3,400 SF lease at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue in North Williamsburg for its first Brooklyn retail location. The space (1,700 SF retail) is positioned in the increasingly popular Williamsburg waterfront corridor near Domino Park and upscale flagship retailers (Rolex, Hermes) on North Sixth Street.
stories.impact: National lifestyle/apparel brand entry into Williamsburg North reflects continued luxury retail densification and high pedestrian traffic in waterfront-adjacent neighborhood. For multifamily developers, this signals sustained demographic strength in North Williamsburg (young professionals, high discretionary income) and rent growth momentum; however, retail expansion often lags residential absorption by 12–24 months, suggesting apartment demand is already priced in. Monitor retail TI costs and co-tenancy risk as Williamsburg retail rents approach Manhattan levels.

stories.title: JLL, NAI Hanson Arrange Sale of Northern NJ IOS Portfolio
stories.excerpt: JLL and NAI James E. Hanson arranged the $68.5-million sale of an industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio located at 2120 McCarter Hwy. in Newark and 76 Central Ave. in Kearny, NJ. JLL also arranged $52.2 million in acquisition financing for the 14.97-acre portfolio on behalf of the buyer, Outpost. NAI Hanson senior managing directors Jordan Avanzato and Christopher Todd, along with managing director William Ericksen of the firm’s Institutional Services Group, Capital Markets & Leasing Team, represented the sellers, Meadow Partners and Criterion Group. For Outpost, JLL managing directors Jason Lundy and Nick Stefans provided representation, along with senior analyst Luke Ceccoli from JLL’s Capital Markets group, as well as vice chairman Dean Brody from JLL’s Brokerage group. Senior managing director Michael Klein, senior director Max Custer and senior analyst Michael Donohoe represented Outpost in securing acquisition financing. “Infill, industrial outdoor storage assets continue to attract institutional capital demand given the supply and demand imbalances,” said Lundy. “This portfolio represents the quality and location of assets that outperform their competitive set.” The post JLL, NAI Hanson Arrange Sale of Northern NJ IOS Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL, NAI Hanson arranged $68.5M sale of 14.97-acre industrial outdoor storage portfolio in NJ.
Portfolio spans Newark (2120 McCarter Hwy.) and Kearny (76 Central Ave.); buyer Outpost.
JLL arranged $52.2M acquisition financing; IOS assets attract institutional capital on supply/demand imbalance.
stories.summary: JLL and NAI James E. Hanson completed the $68.5 million sale of an industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio comprising 2120 McCarter Highway in Newark and 76 Central Avenue in Kearny, NJ, totaling 14.97 acres. Buyer Outpost secured $52.2 million in acquisition financing through JLL. IOS assets continue to attract institutional capital due to supply constraints and demand imbalances.
stories.impact: Northern NJ industrial outdoor storage sale signals institutional investor appetite for niche, supply-constrained logistics assets; IOS demand correlates with construction equipment rental, contractor bases, and industrial activity. For multifamily developers, Northern NJ (Newark, Kearny) continues to attract industrial capital and employment, supporting residential demand in proximate submarkets. However, IOS and logistics uses do not typically generate high-wage job clusters; monitor for lower-wage, shift-based employment that limits rental premiums in redeveloping urban-core NJ markets.

stories.title: CBRE Closes Sale of Shallow-Bay Industrial in New Haven County
stories.excerpt: The CBRE team of Jeff Dunne, Steve Bardsley and Travis Langer in collaboration with Matthew O’Hare of CBRE’s New Haven office completed the $10-million sale of 260-284 Quarry Rd. in Milford, CT. CBRE represented the seller, LM Quarry Road II, LLC, an entity managed by LM Real Estate Partners. CBRE also procured the buyer, Albany Road Strategic Opportunity Fund LLC, an entity managed by Albany Road Real Estate Partners. 260-284 Quarry Rd. is a two-building shallow-bay industrial complex totaling 85,821 square feet and situated on 7.74 acres. It is 100% leased to a diverse tenant roster at below-market rental rates. The property is located proximate to I-95 in New Haven County, which has some of the strongest industrial market fundamentals in Connecticut, according to CBRE. Bardsley said, “260-284 Quarry Rd. is well-positioned in this historically strong market to maintain high occupancy and create upside due to rising rental rates.” The post CBRE Closes Sale of Shallow-Bay Industrial in New Haven County appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE closed $10M sale of 85,821 SF shallow-bay industrial in Milford, CT (New Haven County).
260-284 Quarry Rd. is 100% leased at below-market rents; 7.74 acres proximate to I-95.
Buyer Albany Road Strategic Opportunity Fund; seller LM Real Estate Partners managed asset.
stories.summary: CBRE completed the $10 million sale of 260-284 Quarry Road in Milford, CT, a two-building shallow-bay industrial complex totaling 85,821 SF on 7.74 acres. The property is 100% leased at below-market rents to a diverse tenant roster and is located near I-95 in New Haven County, which CBRE cited as having some of Connecticut's strongest industrial fundamentals.
stories.impact: Below-market leased industrial asset in strong New Haven County submarket attracts value-add buyer (Albany Road SOF), signaling market opportunity for lease renewal/rate-up. For multifamily developers, New Haven County's industrial strength reflects regional logistics corridor activity and stable employment; however, shallow-bay industrial (typically light manufacturing, warehousing) does not generate high-density residential demand. Monitor for intermodal/e-commerce logistics hubs that could drive population growth and residential opportunity in secondary-tier Connecticut submarkets.

stories.title: HealthCore Pays $130M for Six-Building NorthBay Health MOB Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the $130-million sale of the 222,073-square-foot NorthBay Health Medical Outpatient Building Collection, compromised of six fully leased healthcare assets across Fairfield and Vacaville. Co-heads of U.S. Medical Office Capital Markets Ben Appel, Justin Shepherd and Jay Miele, head of healthcare debt John Nero, senior managing director Michael Greeley and associate director Ron Ott advised the seller. The buyer was HealthCore Foundation. “The NorthBay Health Collection represented a rare opportunity to acquire a portfolio of mission-critical healthcare real estate fully occupied by one of Northern California’s leading health systems,” said Appel. “The combination of investment-grade tenancy, long-term lease duration and assets that are deeply integrated within NorthBay Health’s operations made the portfolio highly attractive.” The portfolio is fully leased to NorthBay Health, the dominant health system in the community. The portfolio comprises five medical outpatient facilities and NorthBay Health’s office headquarters, located on and adjacent to major healthcare campuses. The post HealthCore Pays $130M for Six-Building NorthBay Health MOB Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HealthCore Foundation acquired $130M NorthBay Health MOB portfolio (222,073 SF, six buildings).
Portfolio spans Fairfield and Vacaville, CA; 100% leased to NorthBay Health (single tenant).
Medical outpatient facilities plus headquarters; investment-grade tenant, long-term lease, healthcare-integrated assets.
stories.summary: Newmark arranged the $130 million sale of the NorthBay Health Medical Outpatient Building Collection, a six-building portfolio totaling 222,073 SF in Fairfield and Vacaville, California. The portfolio comprises five medical outpatient facilities and NorthBay Health's office headquarters, fully leased to NorthBay Health, the dominant regional health system, on long-term lease terms.
stories.impact: Healthcare REIT/MOB acquisitions reflect institutional preference for mission-critical, investment-grade tenancy and stable, long-duration cash flows. For multifamily developers in Northern California (Fairfield, Vacaville), healthcare system expansion and consolidation signals job growth and professional employment clusters. However, MOB assets are low-density; monitor whether healthcare campus growth correlates with residential demand (e.g., physician/staff housing, senior living, student housing for health professions programs) or simply institutional real estate concentration.

stories.title: ESRT Posts Strong Q3 Office Activity, but Empire State Building Visits Remain Low
stories.excerpt: Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) had a successful third quarter when it comes to office sales and leasing, but that didn’t do much to offset plummeting visitation numbers at the trust’s eponymous Empire State Building. ESRT signed 189,477 square feet of leases during the third quarter of 2026, including 170,608 square feet of office leases, according to the real estate investment trust (REIT)’s earnings report released Tuesday. As of Sept. 30, the REIT’s office portfolio was 91.9 percent occupied, compared to 89.1 percent in the second quarter of this year and 89.7 percent during the third quarter of 2025. Some major office leases signed by ESRT during the third quarter were fintech firm Octaura Holdings’ 28,914-square-foot lease at 111 West 33rd Street. At the Empire State Building, architecture firm Corgan inked a 15,157-square-foot deal and investment firm Zenyth Advisors leased 13,459 square feet. In August, ESRT also sold its 22-story office building at 1359 Broadway in Manhattan’s Midtown South to Thor Equities for $217.5 million, as Commercial Observer first reported. ESRT is redeploying the proceeds of the sale toward share repurchases and to pay down debt. “Over the last five years, we have sold out of suburbs, and began to look at Manhattan assets, where we executed the business plan, and look at sales, and will continue to be active,” Christina Chiu, president of ESRT, said during the firm’s Tuesday afternoon earnings call. “The key objective is cash flow per share as well as value per share, so all those items are on the table, including share buybacks.” The 1359 Broadway sale also came after ESRT sold its 26-story office building at 250 West 57th Street to Namdar Realty Group for roughly $280 million in April. Despite progress on the office front, visitation numbers at the Empire State Building “continued to be weak,” according to the earnings report. bullets: ESRT Q3 2026: 189,477 SF leased (170,608 SF office); 91.9% occupancy, +280 bps QoQ.
Major leases: Octaura 28,914 SF, Corgan 15,157 SF, Zenyth 13,459 SF at ESRT properties.
Empire State Building visitation plummeted; ESRT sold 1359 Broadway to Thor Equities for $217.5M.
stories.summary: Empire State Realty Trust reported strong Q3 2026 office leasing activity (189,477 SF, including Octaura's 28,914 SF lease and Corgan's 15,157 SF expansion) and improved occupancy (91.9%, up 280 bps QoQ to 89.1% in Q2). However, visitation to the Empire State Building declined significantly. ESRT also divested 1359 Broadway to Thor Equities for $217.5 million in August.
stories.impact: ESRT office portfolio strength in Midtown Manhattan reflects tenant confidence in core office demand (fintech, creative services) despite remote-work trends and falling tourism/foot traffic at observation decks. For multifamily developers, this signals divergent market: premium office assets with transit/density anchors remain resilient, while trophy office real estate (Empire State Building) struggles with experiential/tourism value destruction. Expect continued office-to-residential conversion in secondary Midtown assets and outer-borough flight; invest in residential near high-octane office corridors (Herald Square, 5th Ave) to capture office-worker demand.

stories.title: Fintech Firm Octaura Holdings Inks 29K SF at ESRT’s 111 West 33rd Street
stories.excerpt: Octaura Holdings, an electronic trading, data and analytics provider, is moving its offices to 111 West 33rd Street near Midtown Manhattan’s Herald Square. The 28,914-square-foot deal with Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) spans the entire 17th floor of the 26-story office building, the landlord announced Monday. Octaura currently lists its Manhattan headquarters at Haymes Investment Company’s 5 Penn Plaza, but it was not immediately clear whether the company intends to depart that space. Brian Bejile, CEO of Octaura, called the new office “an exciting next chapter” for the company. “As we continue to grow our business and our team, it was important to find a space that reflects where we’re headed and gives our people a great place to collaborate, connect and build together,” Bejile said in a statement. “111 West 33rd Street gives us exactly that, right in the heart of New York City.” Octaura secured a 10-year lease term at the 33rd Street property with an $81 per square foot asking rent, according to an ESRT spokesperson. ESRT’s Shanae Ursini and Kerry Lavelle represented the landlord in-house alongside Newmark‘s Scott Klau, Erik Harris and Neil Rubin. Their Newmark colleagues Neil Goldmacher and Cooper Weisman negotiated on behalf of Octaura. Other tenants in the 728,429-square-foot office tower include delivery app Instacart, which took 26,134 square feet in July, as well as consulting firm Clearview Healthcare Partners and data firm the Penta Group. A spokesperson for Newmark did not respond to a request for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Octaura Holdings leases 28,914 SF full floor at 111 W. 33rd St., $81/SF, 10-year term.
Fintech firm relocating from 5 Penn Plaza; CEO emphasizes collaboration, team growth, city location.
Deal reflects fintech/trading sector confidence in Midtown South Herald Square accessibility.
stories.summary: Octaura Holdings, an electronic trading, data, and analytics firm, signed a 10-year lease for the entire 17th floor (28,914 SF) at 111 West 33rd Street in Midtown South near Herald Square. The asking rent was $81/SF. The firm is reportedly moving from 5 Penn Plaza, citing need for modern space reflecting company growth and team collaboration.
stories.impact: Fintech tenant flight from outer-borough/secondary office to premium Midtown South transit hub signals cluster formation and talent retention priority post-pandemic. For multifamily developers, this reinforces that high-wage fintech and professional services workers demand walkable, transit-rich neighborhoods; Herald Square/Midtown South residential (Chelsea, Flatiron, Nomad) will capture spillover demand and support rent premiums. Monitor for similar moves among tech/fintech firms; each office lease catalyzes 8–12 months of residential lease-up lag in proximate neighborhoods.
